title: Body Fluids and Circulation
syllabus: Composition of blood, blood groups (ABO, Rh), coagulation of blood; Composition of lymph and its function; Human circulatory system - Structure of human heart and blood vessels; Cardiac cycle, cardiac output, ECG, Double circulation; Regulation of cardiac activity; Disorders of circulatory system - Hypertension, Coronary artery disease, Angina pectoris, Heart failure.

questions.question: Which of the following plasma proteins is primarily responsible for maintaining the colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure of blood?
questions.solution: Albumins constitute about 60% of plasma proteins and are primarily responsible for maintaining the colloidal osmotic pressure of blood. Globulins are primarily involved in defense mechanisms (antibodies/immunoglobulins), and fibrins/fibrinogens are needed for blood clotting.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Leukocytes (WBCs) and their characteristic physiological functions/percentages:

List-I (Leukocyte)List-II (Function / Feature)
(A) Neutrophils(I) Secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin; involved in inflammatory reactions (0.5-1%)
(B) Eosinophils(II) Phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms; most abundant WBCs (60-65%)
(C) Basophils(III) Resist infections and are associated with allergic reactions (2-3%)
(D) Monocytes(IV) Large phagocytic agranulocytes that transform into macrophages (6-8%)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Neutrophils: Most abundant (60-65%) and phagocytic; Eosinophils: Resist infections and mediate allergy (2-3%); Basophils: Secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin in inflammation (0.5-1%); Monocytes: Phagocytic agranulocytes (6-8%).

questions.question: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur in a pregnancy if the mating combination and pregnancy involve:
options: An $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ mother carrying an $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ fetus during a second or subsequent pregnancy
questions.solution: Erythroblastosis foetalis occurs when an $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ mother is pregnant with an $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ child. During the delivery of the first child, mixing of blood exposes the mother to $\text{Rh}$ antigens, generating anti-Rh antibodies. In subsequent pregnancies with an $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ fetus, maternal IgG antibodies cross the placenta and destroy fetal RBCs, leading to severe hemolytic anemia and jaundice.

questions.question: Which of the following mineral ions plays a crucial, indispensable cofactor role in multiple steps of the blood clotting cascade?
questions.solution: Calcium ions ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$, Factor IV) play a vital role in blood coagulation, acting as an essential cofactor for the activation of prothrombinase (thrombokinase), conversion of prothrombin to thrombin, and fibrin polymerization.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding ABO blood groups, antigens on RBCs, and antibodies in plasma:

List-I (Blood Group)List-II (Antigens on RBCs & Antibodies in Plasma)
(A) Group A(I) Anti-A and Anti-B antibodies in plasma; no surface antigens
(B) Group B(II) Antigen A on RBCs; Anti-B antibodies in plasma
(C) Group AB(III) Antigen B on RBCs; Anti-A antibodies in plasma
(D) Group O(IV) Both Antigens A and B on RBCs; no antibodies in plasma

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Group A has antigen A and anti-B antibody; Group B has antigen B and anti-A antibody; Group AB has both antigens A & B and no antibodies (universal recipient); Group O has neither antigen and both anti-A & anti-B antibodies (universal donor).

questions.question: An enzyme complex required for the conversion of inactive plasma prothrombin into active thrombin during blood coagulation is:
questions.solution: A cascade of enzymatic reactions initiated by platelets or damaged tissue culminates in the formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase (prothrombinase), which converts inactive prothrombin to active thrombin in the presence of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Lymph (tissue fluid)?
options: Lymph contains more proteins and higher RBC count than blood.
Lymph is a colorless fluid containing specialized lymphocytes responsible for immune responses.
Fats are absorbed through lymph in the lacteals present in the intestinal villi.
Lymph has the same mineral distribution as that found in interstitial fluid.
questions.solution: Lymph is completely devoid of RBCs (making it colorless) and contains less protein compared to blood plasma. It contains specialized lymphocytes and serves as an important carrier for nutrients, hormones, and dietary fats (absorbed via lacteals in intestinal villi).

questions.question: The Sino-Atrial Node (SAN) is called the natural pacemaker of the human heart because it:
options: Generates the maximum number of action potentials (70-75 per minute) and initiates the rhythmic contraction
Prevents backflow of blood between right atrium and ventricle
Directly pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta
Delays electrical impulses to allow ventricles to contract first
questions.solution: The SAN (located in the upper right corner of the right atrium) has inherent auto-rhythmicity and generates the highest frequency of action potentials (70-75/min), initiating and maintaining the rhythmic contractile activity of the heart, thus acting as the pacemaker.

questions.question: The bicuspid (mitral) valve and tricuspid valve guard which of the following openings in the human heart respectively?
options: Left atrio-ventricular opening and Right atrio-ventricular opening
Right atrio-ventricular opening and Left atrio-ventricular opening
Opening of right ventricle into pulmonary artery and left ventricle into aorta
Opening of superior and inferior vena cava into right atrium
questions.solution: The tricuspid valve (with three muscular cusps) guards the right atrio-ventricular orifice, while the bicuspid or mitral valve (with two cusps) guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of a standard Electrocardiogram (ECG):

List-I (ECG Wave)List-II (Electrical / Mechanical Event)
(A) P-wave(I) Repolarisation of ventricles (return from excited to normal state)
(B) QRS complex(II) Depolarisation of atria (leads to atrial contraction)
(C) T-wave(III) Depolarisation of ventricles (initiates ventricular contraction)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: P-wave represents electrical depolarisation of atria; QRS complex represents depolarisation of ventricles (beginning of ventricular systole); T-wave represents ventricular repolarisation. Counting the number of QRS complexes in a given time gives the heart rate.

questions.question: The cardiac output of a healthy adult human with a stroke volume of $70\text{ mL}$ and a heart rate of $72\text{ beats/min}$ is approximately:
questions.solution: $$\text{Cardiac Output} = \text{Stroke Volume (SV)} \times \text{Heart Rate (HR)} = 70\text{ mL} \times 72\text{ beats/min} = 5040\text{ mL/min} \approx 5\text{ L/min}$$

questions.question: The first heart sound ('LUB') and the second heart sound ('DUB') are associated with which mechanical events of the cardiac cycle respectively?
options: Closure of AV valves (tricuspid/bicuspid) and Closure of semilunar valves
Closure of semilunar valves and Closure of AV valves
Opening of AV valves and Opening of semilunar valves
Contraction of atria and Contraction of ventricles
questions.solution: The first heart sound ('lub') is produced by the simultaneous closure of atrioventricular (bicuspid and tricuspid) valves during the onset of ventricular systole. The second heart sound ('dub') is produced by the closure of the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary) at the beginning of ventricular diastole.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the regulation of cardiac activity:
Statement I: Sympathetic neural signals increase the rate of heartbeat, the strength of ventricular contraction, and the cardiac output.
Statement II: Parasympathetic neural signals (via the vagus nerve) decrease the heart rate, speed of conduction of action potentials, and cardiac output.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The autonomic nervous system regulates heart activity through the medulla oblongata: sympathetic nerves release noradrenaline to increase heart rate and force of contraction, while parasympathetic nerves release acetylcholine to decrease heart rate and conduction speed.

questions.question: A unique vascular arrangement in which a vein begins as capillaries in one organ and breaks up into capillaries in another organ before delivering blood to the systemic circulation is known as a:
questions.solution: A portal system is a vascular connection where a capillary bed drains into a vein (portal vein), which then breaks up into a second capillary network in another organ (e.g., the hepatic portal vein carries blood from intestine capillaries to liver sinusoids).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the histological layers of blood vessel walls:

List-I (Tunic / Layer)List-II (Tissue Composition)
(A) Tunica intima(I) Smooth muscle and elastic fibers; comparatively thin in veins
(B) Tunica media(II) Inner lining of squamous endothelium
(C) Tunica externa(III) Outer layer of fibrous connective tissue with collagen fibers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Tunica intima: Inner layer of squamous endothelium; Tunica media: Middle layer of smooth muscle and elastic fibers (thicker in arteries than in veins); Tunica externa: Outer layer of fibrous connective tissue with collagen fibers.

questions.question: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is clinically diagnosed when a patient's repeated blood pressure measurements are consistently at or above:
questions.solution: Normal blood pressure is $120/80\text{ mm Hg}$ (where $120\text{ mm Hg}$ is systolic/pumping pressure and $80\text{ mm Hg}$ is diastolic/resting pressure). Repeated measurements of $140/90\text{ mm Hg}$ or higher indicate hypertension.

questions.question: A symptom of acute chest pain that appears when insufficient oxygen reaches the heart muscles is known as:
questions.solution: Angina (angina pectoris) is characterized by acute chest pain resulting from myocardial ischemia when insufficient oxygen reaches the heart muscle. It can occur in both men and women of any age but is more common among middle-aged and elderly individuals.

questions.question: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD), commonly referred to as atherosclerosis, is caused by the deposition of:
options: Calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissues in the lumen of coronary arteries
Excess glucose inside the coronary sinus
Blood clots in the pulmonary veins exclusively
Urea crystals in the pericardial fluid
questions.solution: Atherosclerosis (CAD) affects the blood vessels that supply oxygenated blood to the heart musculature. It is caused by the deposition of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissues, which narrows the arterial lumen.

questions.question: Heart failure is clinically distinguished from cardiac arrest and heart attack because heart failure is defined as:
options: The state of the heart when it is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the metabolic needs of the body
When the heart suddenly stops beating completely
When the heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply
Complete rupture of the interventricular septum
questions.solution: Heart failure means the state of the heart when it fails to pump blood effectively to meet the body's metabolic requirements (often called congestive heart failure due to lung congestion). Cardiac arrest occurs when the heart stops beating, and a heart attack occurs when the myocardium suffers ischemic necrosis.

questions.question: During a single cardiac cycle lasting $0.8\text{ seconds}$ in a resting human, what is the duration of joint diastole (when all four chambers are in a relaxed state)?
questions.solution: A cardiac cycle lasts $0.8\text{ s}$: Atrial systole $= 0.1\text{ s}$; Ventricular systole $= 0.3\text{ s}$; Joint diastole (when both atria and ventricles are relaxed simultaneously) $= 0.4\text{ s}$.

questions.question: The nodal musculature of the heart has the capability to generate action potentials without any external stimuli because it is:
options: Neurogenic and stimulated directly by somatic motor nerves
Controlled solely by skeletal muscle fibers
questions.solution: The specialized human cardiac conduction system (SAN, AVN, Bundle of His, Purkinje fibers) is autoexcitable, generating rhythmic action potentials intrinsically without external neural input. Hence, the human heart is termed myogenic.

questions.question: Which of the following blood vessels carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle into the lungs for oxygenation?
questions.solution: The pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle and transports deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.question: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments produced in the bone marrow from specialized giant cells called:
questions.solution: Platelets (150,000 to 350,000 per $\text{mm}^3$ of blood) are non-nucleated cell fragments produced by the fragmentation of giant bone marrow cells called megakaryocytes.

questions.question: Serum is defined biochemically as:
options: Blood without formed elements and albumins
Plasma with excess fibrinogen and heparin
questions.solution:
$$\text{Serum} = \text{Blood Plasma} - \text{Clotting Factors (such as fibrinogen)}$$
It is the pale-yellow fluid that remains after blood has clotted.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the specialized cardiac conduction tissue and their anatomical locations:

List-I (Nodal Tissue)List-II (Anatomical Position)
(A) Sino-Atrial Node (SAN)(I) Lower-left corner of right atrium close to atrioventricular septum
(B) Atrio-Ventricular Node (AVN)(II) Upper-right corner of right atrium near opening of superior vena cava
(C) Purkinje fibers(III) Distributed throughout ventricular myocardium forming terminal arborizations

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: SAN: Upper right corner of right atrium; AVN: Lower left corner of right atrium near AV septum; Purkinje fibers: Fine specialized conducting fibers distributed throughout the ventricular walls.

questions.question: During the joint diastole of the cardiac cycle, approximately what percentage of ventricular filling occurs passively before atrial contraction?
questions.solution: During joint diastole, blood flows passively from the pulmonary veins and vena cavae through open AV valves into the ventricles, accounting for about 70% of ventricular filling. Atrial systole pumps the remaining 30% of blood into the ventricles.

questions.question: Which of the following adrenal medullary hormones can increase heart rate, strength of cardiac contraction, and cardiac output during stress/emergency?
questions.solution: Adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline and noradrenaline) stimulate $\beta_1$-adrenergic receptors on the heart, increasing heart rate, cardiac contractility, and cardiac output.

questions.question: The volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle during one cardiac cycle (systole) is termed:
questions.solution: During each cardiac cycle, each ventricle pumps out approximately $70\text{ mL}$ of blood, which is called the stroke volume.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Fishes possess a 2-chambered heart with single circulation.
Statement II: Amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) possess a 3-chambered heart with incomplete double circulation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Fishes have a 2-chambered heart (one atrium, one ventricle) exhibiting single circulation. Amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) have a 3-chambered heart (two atria, one ventricle) where oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the single ventricle (incomplete double circulation). Birds and mammals have 4-chambered hearts with complete double circulation.

questions.question: In a standard 12-lead diagnostic ECG setup, how many electrical leads are attached to a patient's limbs for baseline monitoring?
options: 3 electrical leads (one to each wrist and one to the left ankle)
4 leads (one to each wrist and one to each ankle)
questions.solution: For a standard baseline limb-lead ECG, a patient is connected to the machine with three electrical leads: one attached to each wrist (right and left) and one attached to the left ankle.

questions.question: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood directly to the heart musculature?
questions.solution: A specialized system of coronary blood vessels (left and right coronary arteries arising from the root of the ascending aorta) is dedicated exclusively to supplying oxygenated blood to the cardiac musculature.

questions.question: A reduction in the number of blood platelets (thrombocytopenia) leads to:
options: Clotting disorders and excessive loss of blood from the body
Increased risk of blood thrombus formation
questions.solution: Platelets release a variety of clotting factors. A drop in platelet count (below normal $1.5-3.5 \times 10^5/\text{mm}^3$) causes coagulation defects and leads to spontaneous bleeding and purpura.

questions.question: Which of the following valves prevents the backflow of blood from the pulmonary artery and aorta into the right and left ventricles during ventricular diastole?
questions.solution: The openings of the right and left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and aorta respectively are guarded by semilunar (half-moon shaped) valves that prevent the backflow of blood into the ventricles during diastole.

questions.question: Average life span of human red blood corpuscles (erythrocytes) is approximately $120\text{ days}$, after which they are destroyed in the:
questions.solution: Mature human RBCs have an average lifespan of about 120 days. Old and worn-out erythrocytes are phagocytosed by macrophages in the spleen, which is termed the 'graveyard of RBCs'.

questions.question: In humans, an opening between the right and left atria during fetal development that normally closes at birth is called:
questions.solution: The foramen ovale is an aperture in the interatrial septum of the fetal heart allowing blood to bypass the non-functioning lungs. At birth, it closes to form a shallow depression called the fossa ovalis.

questions.question: Which granulocyte with a multi-lobed nucleus and neutral-staining granules constitutes the first line of defense during acute bacterial infection?
questions.solution: Neutrophils (polymorphonuclear leukocytes/PMNLs) have 3-5 lobed nuclei and neutral granules. They are active phagocytes that migrate quickly to infection sites to engulf bacterial pathogens.

questions.question: The cardiac cycle begins with atrial systole. Atrial systole increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about:
questions.solution: The action potential from the SAN causes simultaneous contraction of both atria (atrial systole). This increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent (the remaining 70% enters passively during joint diastole).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the terms related to heart rate and cardiac pathology:

List-I (Condition)List-II (Definition / Diagnostic Feature)
(A) Tachycardia(I) Resting heart rate abnormally slow ($< 60\text{ beats/min}$)
(B) Bradycardia(II) Resting heart rate abnormally fast ($> 100\text{ beats/min}$)
(C) Heart attack(III) Sudden death of heart muscle due to insufficient coronary blood supply
(D) Cardiac arrest(IV) Heart completely stops pumping and electrical activity ceases

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Tachycardia: Abnormally elevated heart rate ($>100\text{ bpm}$); Bradycardia: Abnormally slow heart rate ($<60\text{ bpm}$); Heart attack (myocardial infarction): Ischemic necrosis of heart muscle; Cardiac arrest: Complete cessation of heartbeat.

questions.question: In an open circulatory system (as found in Arthropods and Molluscs):
options: Blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open body cavities or spaces called sinuses
Blood is confined entirely within closed muscular tubes and capillary networks
Heart and respiratory pigment are completely absent
Blood pressure is extremely high and tightly regulated
questions.solution: In an open circulatory system (arthropods, non-cephalopod molluscs), blood is pumped by the heart into large open tissue spaces and sinuses (hemocoel), directly bathing the organs. Closed circulatory systems (annelids, cephalopods, vertebrates) circulate blood within a closed network of vessels.

questions.question: A person with blood group AB is called a universal recipient because their blood contains:
options: Both A and B antigens on RBC surface and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma
Neither A nor B antigens on RBCs and both antibodies in plasma
Anti-A and Anti-B antibodies but no Rh factor
Only antigen A on RBCs and no antibodies
questions.solution: Individuals with AB blood group have both antigen A and antigen B on their erythrocytes and lack anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma, so they can safely receive blood of any ABO group.

questions.question: The bundle of His is a group of specialized cardiac muscle fibers that originates from the ________ and passes through the ________:
questions.solution: The atrioventricular bundle (bundle of His) arises from the AV node, traverses the atrioventricular septum, emerges at the top of the interventricular septum, and divides into right and left bundle branches.

questions.question: The lumen of an artery is narrower than that of a corresponding vein because:
options: Tunica media is much thicker with more smooth muscle and elastic fibers in arteries
Arteries have valves that constrict the lumen
Tunica externa is completely absent in arteries
Arteries carry deoxygenated blood under low pressure
questions.solution: Arteries carry blood under high pulsating pressure from the heart and possess a much thicker muscular and elastic middle layer (tunica media), giving them a narrower lumen compared to veins.

questions.question: What is the normal count of white blood corpuscles (WBCs) per cubic millimeter ($\text{mm}^3$) in a healthy human adult?
questions.solution: Leukocytes (WBCs) are nucleated cells averaging $6000 - 8000\text{ per mm}^3$ of blood. ($4.5-5.5\text{ million/mm}^3$ is the RBC count; $1.5-3.5 \times 10^5/\text{mm}^3$ is the platelet count).

questions.question: During the ventricular ejection period of the cardiac cycle, blood is pumped into:
options: Pulmonary artery from right ventricle and Systemic aorta from left ventricle
Pulmonary veins from right ventricle and Vena cava from left ventricle
questions.solution: During ventricular systole, high intraventricular pressure forces open the semilunar valves, ejecting blood from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery (pulmonary circulation) and from the left ventricle into the systemic aorta (systemic circulation).

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Hepatic portal vein carries blood from intestine to the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation.
Statement II: Coronary circulation is a system of blood vessels that supplies blood exclusively to the cardiac musculature.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The hepatic portal vein drains nutrient-rich blood from the gut into the liver for metabolism and detoxication. The coronary circulation supplies oxygenated blood to the heart wall and returns deoxygenated blood to the right atrium via the coronary sinus.
